subject: Re: Order Form — invoice recipient, VAT handling, and min-commit staircase
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@finora.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finora.com>, finance@finora.com
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2024 15:45:00 +0000
Subject: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Soojin, thanks for sending the updated order form. A few quick items from procurement/finance that we need clarified before we can sign: 

1) Invoice recipient / entity: our legal ops requires invoices to be issued to Finora EU Ltd (GB subsidiary). The copy you sent lists Redwood Inc as the billing entity and our AP team is asking for a route that invoices can be sent to Finora EU Ltd. Can you confirm whether Redwood can route invoices to the EU entity or whether we need a separate SOW/order for the EU entity?

2) VAT handling: as this is a cross-border service, do you accept reverse-charge for VAT in the UK/EU? If yes, we need your VAT number and a clause explicitly stating reverse-charge will be applied where applicable. If no, we need the gross amount and will handle VAT on our side — but that affects how our treasury reconciles.

3) Minimum commit staircase: procurement has asked for a clearer billing cadence on the min-commit staircase (Year 1 100k, Year 2 150k, Year 3 200k). They want to understand whether the invoices will be issued monthly/quarterly and whether unused commit is subject to prorations/true-ups at year-end.

Attached: our suggested redlines (Finora_OrderForm_v3.pdf) and the pricing breakdown (Pricing_Staircase_20240610.xlsx). Please loop in legal if the routing needs a contract amendment. 

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Procurement — Finora

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@finora.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Jun 2024 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below and then next steps.

1) Invoice recipient / entity: We can support invoicing to Finora EU Ltd as a billing recipient (AP email and remit-to). However, because Redwood Inc is the contracting entity in the current MSA, well need an Order Form appendix that records the invoice recipient and billing entity mapping (so accounting gets the right remit). That appendix is paperwork-only (no change to the primary contracting party) — happy to provide a template.

2) VAT / reverse-charge: Redwood has a UK VAT registration (GB999888777). We are able to support reverse-charge where customer is VAT-registered and its applicable; we will include an explicit VAT clause if you confirm Finora EU Ltds VAT ID. If Finora wants Redwood to bill gross (no reverse-charge), we can do that too but it will change the net amounts on invoices.

3) Min-commit staircase invoicing: We generally invoice monthly for committed amounts (pro-rata each month based on annual commit) with a year-end true-up. Unused commit is credited back or rolled forward depending on the selected billing option — we can support either: credit note at year-end or roll-forward for 90 days. Sizing and proration rules are in the Pricing_Staircase_20240610.xlsx attached.

Next steps: ben (ccd) will draft the short Order Form appendix that sets the invoice remit-to mapping and billing cadence. Kimberly, can legal confirm whether an appendix (non-substantive) is acceptable given the MSA currently names Redwood Inc as the contracting party?

Ill also send a version of the order form that lists Finora EU Ltd as the invoice recipient but keeps Redwood Inc as the contracting party.

Thanks,
Soojin
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Jun 2024 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Soojin / Ben — quick legal take:

- We can accept an "Invoice Recipient" appendix that maps the billing remit-to without altering the contracting party. That appendix must include a statement that tax/legal liability remains with Redwood Inc (unless we execute an amendment making Finora EU Ltd a contracting party).

- Reverse-charge: we will include a short VAT clause that enables reverse-charge where the customer provides a VAT ID and confirms theyre VAT-registered for cross-border services. We cannot unilaterally apply reverse-charge without the customers VAT ID.

- Minimum commit / proration: suggest we include a line that invoices will be issued monthly based on pro-rated committed yearly amounts, with a year-end true-up and credit note for overpayment or option to roll-forward for up to 90 days. Also add language capping the roll-forward to ensure no indefinite liability.

Action items for Ben: draft appendix language and updated order form (PDF + clean Word). Keep the amendment light — procurement prefers minimal legal friction.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Soto <elena@finora.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finora.com>, finance@finora.com
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2024 11:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Order form questions — invoice recipient and VAT

Thanks Soo / Kim / Ben — this works. Finora EU Ltd VAT ID is GB123456789. We prefer reverse-charge on cross-border services; can you reflect that in the appendix and send back a redline we can route to our legal ops? Also Tom in finance would like monthly invoices with a year-end true-up and credit note option (roll-forward is a secondary preference).

If you can send the updated Order Form + appendix (PDF + clean Word) and a DocuSign link, well aim to get signatures by the end of next week.

Regards,
Elena Soto
Director, Procurement — Finora
